We have carbon NMR shifts list. Need number of CH3 groups (methyl). Identify which carbons correspond to methyl groups. Typically methyl carbon chemical shift around 10-30 ppm for aliphatic, maybe 15-30 for sp3 attached to heteroatoms, 50-60 for O-CH3 (methoxy) etc. In list we have: 166.40 (carbonyl), 144.78 (aromatic sp2), 132.00,130.07,130.07,127.80,127.80 (aromatic), 52.24,49.55,43.55,19.23.

The low shift 19.23 likely a methyl (alkyl). 52.24 could be O-CH3 (methoxy) also methyl attached to O. 49.55 maybe CH2? 43.55 maybe CH? But we need number of CH3 groups. Could be two methyls: one at 19.23 (maybe a simple alkyl methyl) and one at 52.24 (methoxy). Need confirm via proton NMR maybe. Let's get proton NMR.
